haiku-low.q1: Reports of 10,000 rows or fewer stream CSV in the click response. Larger reports queue a background job; the user later gets an emailed 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q2: It returns that existing queued or running export instead of creating another one.
haiku-low.q3: The link works for 24 hours (86,400 seconds). The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation; no cleanup job is needed.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts maximum. After the third fails, status becomes failed, the user gets a failure email, and can start a new export.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. Rows are read from the read replica, never from the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: The report_exports row, in the primary database. The page reads it from the latest-export endpoint on open or click, polling while queued or running.
haiku-low.q7: Reads the replica 500 rows at a time, uploading 5 MB multipart parts as they fill. Only one batch and one part are in memory.
haiku-low.q8: An error tries to abort the upload; a dead worker skips that, and the bucket drops it within 24 hours. The next attempt starts over.
haiku-low.q9: Saved in the report_exports row at click time. The job payload holds only the export id; the job reads filters from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A unique index on the table allows one queued or running row per user and report; a second insert gets the first row back.
haiku-low.q11: The upload must complete first, then a signed link is emailed. If the row is already done, the job stops.
haiku-low.q12: The response is cut off partway through. The browser should not save it as complete, and the user must click Download CSV again.

sonnet.q1: By reads of reports.row_count: 10,000 or fewer rows streams the CSV directly in the response to the click; more than 10,000 is built by a background job, which writes the CSV to object storage and emails the user a link (valid 24 hours). The page shows the state of a large export.
sonnet.q2: The existing queued or running export is returned (a unique index allows only one queued/running row per user and report); no new export is created.
sonnet.q3: The link works 24 hours (86,400 seconds). The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after it was created; no cleanup job is needed.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (waits of 60 s and 300 s before attempts 2 and 3). After the third fails, on_final_failure sets status to failed and sends a failure email; the page shows failed, and the user can start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica, never the primary database.
sonnet.q6: In the status column of the report_exports row in the primary database. The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest, polling every few seconds while queued or running; on reopening it calls that endpoint again and reads the latest row.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads 500 rows at a time from the replica, builds CSV parts of at least 5 MB, uploads each part via multipart upload as it fills, so only one batch and one part are in memory. Whether 2 million rows finish within the 30-minute attempt limit is an open question; if not, the job must be split and the plan does not say how.
sonnet.q8: The attempt tries to abort its multipart upload; uploaded parts are invisible in the bucket (nothing visible at the key until completion). If the worker dies, no abort runs and the bucket discards the unfinished upload within 24 hours. The next attempt starts from the beginning with a new upload.
sonnet.q9: In the report_exports row (filters and columns stored with the user and report) in the primary database. The job payload is only the export id, and the job loads the row to get the stored filters.
sonnet.q10: A unique index on report_exports allowing only one queued or running row per user and report; the second request gets the first row back.
sonnet.q11: The upload must be completed (file appears at its key) and a signed link created before send_email is called; status is set to done after the email. If the queue runs the job again and the row is already done, the job stops. If the file was finished and email sent but the row was not yet marked done, a retry restarts from step 4 and sends the email again (duplicate accepted, at-least-once delivery).
sonnet.q12: The server stops partway through the response, so the response is cut off; the browser should not save the file as complete. The user sees an incomplete download and clicks again.
